bp-0008 SOURCE-SURFACE JUDGEMENT, PERFORMED EXPLICITLY AND ON THE RECORD. core has nothing at all: no std::env, std::fs, std::net, std::process, no thread, no async, no unsafe, no FFI, sole dependency serde, forbid(unsafe_code). sdk has exactly one I/O call in the whole crate, File::open in fs.rs, reached only from ConfigSource::File after an absolute-path check, bounded to max_bytes plus one, with metadata taken from the open handle rather than the path so there is no TOCTOU window; zero environment reads, zero network, zero process launches, no threads, no async, forbid(unsafe_code). cli has zero ambient reads, every context value arrives through CliContext and writers are caller-owned. app is the imperative shell and the only place ambient state is read: env::current_dir, env::args_os and the compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION, which is exactly where a composition root should read it.

Dependency surface corroborates the judgement: the shipped closure from the manifests is serde, serde_json, clap and clap's rendering crates; tempfile and unisphere-testkit are dev-only and testkit is publish = false; no build.rs exists anywhere in the workspace. unisphere-arch-check enforces this kind-aware against cargo metadata --locked on DECLARED edges, so an optional or target-specific dependency cannot slip past on a machine that never builds it, and internal edges must use a local path so a registry substitute cannot impersonate an internal contract.

Sealed hostile-environment behaviour is real rather than decorative: sealed_command clears the environment, sets PATH to empty and redirects HOME/XDG/TMP into a temporary root, and hostile_consumer then runs the external SDK consumer four times, baseline plus HOME-poisoned plus XDG-poisoned plus UNISPHERE_CONFIG/UNISPHERE_CONFIG_PATH/UNISPHERE_SOURCE_ROOTS/UNISPHERE_OUTPUT-poisoned, with an ambient-must-not-win document planted at three plausible discovery paths, and requires byte-identical stdout across all four.

Proof tooling drives production rather than fixtures: it builds a genuine external Cargo project from a template with a runtime-resolved SDK path, builds unisphere-app with --locked, and performs a real cargo install --locked --path crates/app --root into a temporary root before invoking the installed binary from outside the checkout. require_file refuses every lane when a target is absent and absent_targets_fail_before_any_build asserts all three lanes fail with 'required target absent' while leaving the scratch directory uncreated, so a placeholder or the baseline core/testkit suite cannot satisfy composition.

The diagnostic-leak assertion is NOT vacuous, which I checked specifically: machine() rejects any stdout containing SENSITIVE-CONFIG-MARKER, and that marker really is embedded in malformed.json, UNKNOWN_KEY and INVALID_UTF8, so hostile bytes genuinely flow through the parser on every run. machine() also rejects non-JSON, extra newlines, stderr contamination, wrong ok/error discrimination and non-actionable errors; child failures retain status, stdout and stderr.
